title: Model event-driven state machines as tasks
summary: A task naturally owns state and serializes the messages which represent its events.
recommendation: Start an event-driven state machine as a task whose accepted messages describe events and whose private value describes the current state.
rationale: Task isolation makes event ordering and state ownership explicit while keeping transitions close to the messages which trigger them.
confidence: High confidence that the task has no syntactically explicit state update in a message handler; the syntax view does not resolve indirect transitions through called functions.
exceptions: Prefer a pure transition function when no persistent task identity, asynchronous event source, or isolated mutable state is required.
